newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian dollar closes easier, Friday seen quiet.
newsitem.headline: Canadian dollar closes easier, Friday seen quiet.

text.p: * Canada's dollar ended easier at C$1.3453 (US$0.7433) in active dealings from Wednesday's close of C$1.3436 (US$0.7443). * Some investors took profits today by selling the unit after its recent strengths. * Trading seen quiet on Friday as protests planned against Ontario's Conservative government in Toronto. * Unit seen floating in mid-range overnight.
Strong long-term economic fundamentals and the federal government's determination to cut the deficit have convinced investors that Canada's dollar should continue to appreciate.
The dollar is likely to bounce in the range of C$1.3425 to C$1.3475 overnight, Gregory said.

Both agreed that foreign exchange trading will be quiet in Canada's busiest economic centre on Friday, as protestors plan to shut down Toronto traffic to demonstrate against deep budget cuts by Ontario's Conservative government.
"Tomorrow is going to be a very thin day," Gregory said.
"People are kind of freaked out," Cieplucha said. Some traders will take the day off while some others made arrangements to start travelling early to avoid the anticipated traffic.
On the crosses today, the Canadian dollar sank to 1.1273 marks from Wednesday's close of 1.1318 marks and eased to 83.82 yen from 84.01 yen.
